note: Ground truth is a (source_file, chunk_index) pair. Chunk indices restart at 0 for every source file, so an index alone is ambiguous. Questions with more than one acceptable chunk exist for two distinct reasons. Seven audio questions: the audio chunker uses ~50% overlap, so the same sentence genuinely lives in two adjacent chunks and retrieving either is correct. One PDF question (Q19): the PDF chunker does NOT overlap, and it split a passage mid-argument so the answer straddles two chunks - see that entry's note. single_gt marks the questions with exactly one acceptable chunk; those are the real discriminators, and the multi_gt subset should be read as the easier bucket rather than as evidence about the retriever.

questions.note: Ground truth widened from [12] to [12, 13] after the all-MiniLM-L6-v2 baseline run. Chunk 13 ('the learner controls the sequence of training examples ... the learner might rely on the teacher to select informative board states') answers this question as directly as chunk 12 does. Unlike the audio chunker, the PDF chunker does not overlap, so it split the passage mid-argument and the original single ground truth landed on the wrong half. This is a chunk-boundary labelling artifact, not a retrieval result. The correction was made before any model comparison, so every model is scored against the same question set; the baseline results file was regenerated against the corrected set.
